subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Should maintainers require live or deterministic proof of a healthy processing run reaching stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run before changing the processing/no-activeWorkKind recovery policy?
rationale: Current source and tests show the reported fallthrough, but the false healthy-run abort is not confirmed and the linked Track B PR changes broader liveness behavior.

options.title: Require proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open under the liveness track until a targeted harness, log, or live run proves the false-abort path and the chosen fix preserves real stale recovery.

options.title: Approve standalone guard
options.body: Ask for a narrow patch that defers recovery after delayed heartbeat ticks or processing/no-activeWorkKind states, with regression coverage for genuine stale sessions.

options.title: Resolve through Track B
options.body: Treat the open evidence-based liveness PR as the only implementation path once its review finding, proof gap, and stacked dependency are resolved.

recommendation.title: Require proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open under the liveness track until a targeted harness, log, or live run proves the false-abort path and the chosen fix preserves real stale recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the open lifecycle design and Track B PR that already scopes this issue's event-loop stall liveness concern.
